text:
Alice M: FYI onboarding Zephyr-13B into staging — ran tokenizer conversion (sentencepiece -> gpt2-bpe) and hit a huge <unk> increase + downstream embed mismatch on eval set. attaching logs below. anyone seen this pattern?

Ben K: Oof. Is Zephyr using a different normalization (NFKC/NFC) or special merges?

Alice M: I diffed vocab headers: Zephyr's sp model has legacy normalizer entries. Command I used:
```
python tools/convert_sp_to_bpe.py --sp model/sentencepiece.model --out vocab.json --norm nfkc
```
Got warnings about reserved tokens and then 12% unk on longform-wiki split.

Carla S: 12% is huge. Did you also run an embedding-stability check? Maybe token ids shifted causing wrong embedding lookup.

Alice M: Yep, ran cosine sim between converted-embeddings and original (float32 baseline) — mean sim 0.62 vs typical 0.98. Suspect token id aliasing / offset.

Dmitri P: Could be token aliasing. Some SP -> BPE converters collapse characters differently and reorder tokens. Try printing first 200 token->string mappings from both tokenizers and diff. I had a similar hit when onboarding Mistral-fork that used nonstandard pad id.

Alice M: Good idea. quick diff:
```
# from Zephyr converted vocab[0..200]
0: <pad>
1: <s>
2: </s>
3: the
4: ,
...
# baseline Gemma vocab[0..200]
0: <unk>
1: the
2: ,
3: .
```
So pad shifted into id0 on Zephyr which cascaded.

Ben K: That explains embedding misalignment. Fix is to remap ids to match our serving embedding order or rebuild embeddings with new order. Quick patch: produce an id_remap.json and run token-bot to reindex.

Alice M: I tried remapping and re-quantizing weights (llama-family int8 recipe). After remap+requant int8, quality recovered but quant regressed on long-context PPL: float32 PPL 12.4 -> int8 16.8 (was expecting ~13.2).

Carla S: Any differences in rotary/rope params? Zephyr's model_card shows headwise_rope_scale = 1.15 vs our Gemma baseline 1.0. If rotary scaling is headwise and we assume global scale, kv cache alignment can break and degrade generative quality, especially with quantization noise.

Dmitri P: Good call. Also check whether Zephyr exported attention as interleaved QKV layout; our kernel selection picks different matmul paths and quantization error amplifies. Run this quick check:
```bash
python eng/ml/check_model_layout.py --model Zephyr-13B --report rotary,layout,quant_bias
```

Eva (infra): CI note — that check job is queued on staging-gpu-12, ETA ~2m.

token-bot: job 42109 finished: rotary=HEADWISE(1.15), layout=QKV_INTERLEAVED, quant_bias=0.7

Alice M: Results confirm headwise rope + interleaved QKV. Suggestions?

Ben K: Two paths: 1) re-export model with global rope scaling to match our runtime assumptions, or 2) adapt runtime to detect headwise rope and apply per-head scaling when loading (we have a draft patch in runtime to support headwise-rope but not fully tested under int8). For immediate unblock, re-export is faster if upstream accepts.

Carla S: For quant regression: try per-channel scale calibration for int8 QKV matmuls and enable asymmetric quant for bias. I pushed a calibration script earlier (eng-ml/tools/quant_calibrate.py) that helped with Qwen variants.

Alice M: I'll try remap + per-channel calibration + enable runtime headwise-rope flag. Planning to run three quick benchmarks: wiki-long PPL, winograd-latency, and end-to-end throughput (batch=1). ETA ~45m.

Dmitri P: Please capture tokenization smoke tests too: run decode for edge-cases (emoji, CJK, long URLs) — tokenizer differences sometimes only show up there.

Alice M: Will do. Posting results when done. thanks! :thumbsup:

Ben K: if you need someone to ping upstream Zephyr maintainers for a re-export, I can do that.

Alice M: appreciated. I'll hold off full rollout until we have int8 parity within 10% of float PPL.

Carla S: If re-export not possible, we should add a conversion checklist item: verify special tokens order, normalize NFKC, check rope scalars, and run quant calibration. Save to onboarding checklist doc.

Alice M: noted — adding to ENG-ML onboarding checklist.
